summary: Gate T4 proof: ACE (TypeScript, ace-residency-policy.ts) decides tile residency by utility score; GpuTileCache (Python) physically promotes/evicts on the real RTX 3060 Ti. Decision crosses the process boundary as plain JSON, matching the wire-format layering rule (JSON describes the decision; tensors are never serialized through it).

gpuSideExecution.backend: GpuTileCache (real pinned-memory -> async-H2D staging onto cuda:0, RTX 3060 Ti)

attempt1_naive_descending_promotion_orde.description: Promoted tiles in ACE's utility-descending order (highest utility promoted first) -- the naive/natural reading of 'promote ACE's ranked tiles'.
attempt1_naive_descending_promotion_orde.rootCause: GpuTileCache is a plain LRU cache (OrderedDict, victim = oldest non-pinned insertion). Its docstring says 'ACE should rank/promote tiles before calling this backend,' meaning the caller must promote in ASCENDING utility order so the highest-utility tile is inserted LAST and is therefore most-recently-used under LRU. Promoting in descending order (the naive reading) inserts the highest-utility tile FIRST, making it the oldest and thus the first eviction victim -- the exact opposite of the intended outcome.
attempt1_naive_descending_promotion_orde.severity: The promotion-order requirement exists only as a docstring comment -- nothing in the type system or a runtime check enforces or verifies it. A first-time caller (this proof included) can silently get exactly backwards residency behavior with no error, no exception, no warning -- the cache just runs cleanly and keeps the wrong tiles resident.

attempt2_fixed_ascending_promotion_order.description: Reversed to promote tiles in ACE's utility-ascending order per the documented convention.

conclusion.whatWasProven: ACE's utility-based residency decision (computed in TypeScript, crossing the process boundary as JSON) correctly and reproducibly determines which tiles physically survive GPU LRU eviction under a real memory budget on real CUDA hardware.
conclusion.gapFoundAndFixedSameDay: The ACE-utility-to-LRU-order translation was a caller responsibility enforced only by a code comment, with zero test coverage on GpuTileCache. Fixed: added GpuTileCache.promote_ranked() (accepts ACE's natural descending-utility order and performs the reversal internally) and python/parent_atlas_tensor/test_gpu_tile_cache.py (3 tests: a regression guard pinning down the old plain-promote() footgun, an exact_cosine()-vs-CPU-oracle test making the Gate T3 proof permanent, and a promote_ranked() correctness test). 12/12 tests pass in this Python package after the fix (up from 0 tests on this module before).

notProven: Real production packet data (synthetic per-tile matrices, seeded deterministically by tile key)
TileDirectory persistence (TensorTileManifest objects were constructed in-memory for this proof, not read from/written to a real TileDirectory implementation)
Concurrent/multi-request residency pressure (this proof is single-threaded, single decision, single promotion pass)
Gate T5 (Valkey/BitFrost metadata mirroring of residency state) and Gate T6 (CAGRA parity)
